name: Pre-Big Bang Dilaton Vacuum
description: A homogeneous, anisotropic universe of low energy string theory whose scale factors are powers of time, $(-t)^{\beta_i}$ with $\sum_i\beta_i^2 = 1$, and whose dilaton changes as the logarithm of $-t$. With every exponent negative it expands faster and faster toward a curvature singularity at $t = 0$, the phase that Maurizio Gasperini and Gabriele Veneziano placed before the big bang.
convention: We use units in which the speed of light is one, and the Ricci tensor is the standard contraction, $R_{\mu\nu} = R^\alpha{}_{\mu\alpha\nu}$.
history:
Gabriele Veneziano extended a symmetry of strings on circles to expanding universes at CERN in 1991 [veneziano1991duality]. A closed string on a circle of radius $R$ is equivalent to one on a circle of radius $\alpha'/R$, with $\alpha'$ the inverse string tension divided by $2\pi$, and this target space duality requires a shift of the dilaton $\phi$ [veneziano1991duality, tseytlin1991dilaton]. Veneziano took a metric $ds^2 = -dt^2 + \sum_i a_i(t)^2dx_i^2$ and a dilaton $\phi(t)$, under the low energy action $\int d^Dx\,\sqrt{-g}\,e^{-\phi}\left(R + \partial_\mu\phi\,\partial^\mu\phiight)$ in $D$ dimensions [veneziano1991duality]. He found its field equations unchanged by $a_i 	o 1/a_i$ and $\phi 	o \phi - 2\ln a_i$, one scale factor at a time [veneziano1991duality]. The map leaves the shifted dilaton $ ar\phi = \phi - \sum_i\ln a_i$ unchanged and reverses the sign of each expansion rate $H_i = \dot a_i/a_i$, so it turns an expanding direction into a contracting one [veneziano1991duality, gasperini2003prebigbang]. Arkady A. Tseytlin, at Johns Hopkins, wrote the same shift of the dilaton that year for a torus whose radii change with time [tseytlin1991dilaton].¶In four dimensions the field equations are $R_{\mu

abla\phi)^2 = 0$ [veneziano1991duality]. On $t < 0$ they are solved by $ds^2 = -dt^2 + \sum_i(-t)^{2 eta_i}dx_i^2$ with $\phi = (\sum_i eta_i - 1)\ln(-t)$ [gasperini2003prebigbang]. Both equations hold exactly when $\sum_i eta_i^2 = 1$, so two of the three exponents are free [gasperini2003prebigbang]. Space is flat and homogeneous at each moment, of Bianchi type I, and the shifted dilaton is $ ar\phi = -\ln(-t)$ for every choice of the exponents [gasperini2003prebigbang]. With $\sum_i eta_i = 1$ the dilaton is constant and the line element is Kasner's vacuum with its time reversed [lidsey2000superstring]. Veneziano learned after finishing his paper that Mark Theodore Mueller had written the general solution in 1990 for the critical bosonic string, with 26 spacetime dimensions [veneziano1991duality, mueller1990rolling].¶The string coupling is $g_s^2 = e^\phi$, which on the approach to $t = 0$ vanishes, settles to a constant, or grows without bound as $\sum_i eta_i$ is greater than, equal to, or less than one [veneziano1991duality, gasperini2003prebigbang]. A direction with nonzero $ eta_i$ has a divergent expansion rate there, and the curvature grows as $1/t^2$ except for $(1, 0, 0)$ and its permutations, which make the spacetime flat [veneziano1991duality, mueller1990rolling]. With every exponent equal to $-1/\sqrt3$ space expands alike in every direction as $a = (-t)^{-1/\sqrt3}$, and the dilaton $\phi = -(1 + \sqrt3)\ln(-t)$ grows with it [gasperini2003prebigbang]. There $\dot a$, $\ddot a$, and $\dot H$ are all positive, an accelerating expansion called superinflation [gasperini2003prebigbang]. Veneziano read these solutions as an evolution from flat space and weak coupling through superinflation to large curvature and strong coupling, and he identified that regime with the big bang [veneziano1991duality]. The semiclassical description ends at the singularity, and Veneziano hoped that in quantum string theory the evolution continues through it to $t > 0$ [veneziano1991duality].¶Maurizio Gasperini, in Turin, and Veneziano built a cosmology on the duality in 1992 [gasperini1993prebigbang]. Time reversal is a second symmetry of the same equations, and with the inversion it acts as $a(t) 	o a^{-1}(-t)$, which carries any decelerating expansion of decreasing curvature on $t > 0$ to an accelerating expansion of growing curvature on $t < 0$ [gasperini1993prebigbang]. Gasperini and Veneziano called "pre-big-bang" any phase of growing curvature and accelerated evolution, and in their picture the big bang is "an instant of maximal curvature marking the transition" from such a phase to the decelerating expansion of the standard cosmology [gasperini1993prebigbang]. They proposed that such a phase produces a background of relic gravitons [gasperini1993prebigbang]. During the initial dilaton vacuum, the energy of these gravitons per logarithmic frequency interval grows as frequency cubed, up to logarithmic corrections [gasperini2003prebigbang]. They expected that, without higher order quantum effects of strings, a singularity at the transition cannot be avoided [gasperini1993prebigbang].¶Duality and time reversal together give each solution four branches, $a(t)$, $a(-t)$, $a^{-1}(t)$, and $a^{-1}(-t)$, two expanding and two contracting [gasperini2003prebigbang]. On two of them the curvature grows toward a singularity, and on the other two it falls away from one [gasperini2003prebigbang]. In the isotropic case, of the two branches with growing curvature only the expanding one has a growing dilaton, so it carries the universe away from the weakly coupled vacuum of the string [gasperini2003prebigbang]. Rescaled from this string frame to the Einstein frame, $	ilde g_{\mu
u} = e^{-\phi}g_{\mu
u}$, where the dilaton is an ordinary massless scalar field, the isotropic superinflation becomes an accelerating contraction, $	ilde a = (-	ilde t)^{1/3}$ in the time $	ilde t$ of that frame, which is the flat universe of a massless scalar field run backward in time [gasperini2003prebigbang]. Gasperini and Veneziano read the two as one scenario in two conformal frames [gasperini2003prebigbang]. For general exponents the Einstein frame geometry is Kasner's universe with a scalar field, with exponents satisfying $\sum_i p_i = 1$ and $\sum_i p_i^2 = 1 - p_\phi^2/2$, where $\phi = p_\phi\ln(-	ilde t) + \phi_0$ [lidsey2000superstring].¶At lowest order the vacuum branches before and after the big bang are disconnected, separated by the singularity at $t = 0$ [gasperini2003prebigbang]. Ram Brustein and Veneziano found in 1994 that negative dilaton potentials can produce a change of branch, but the trajectories they followed returned to the initial branch and failed to reach a decelerating expansion [brustein1994exit]. They called this a "very-hard-to-go theorem" and explicitly left open the possibility of an exception to their argument [brustein1994exit]. They sought an exit at large curvature, where the higher order string corrections enter the dynamics [brustein1994exit].¶Gasperini, Michele Maggiore, and Veneziano obtained a phase of constant curvature and a dilaton linear in cosmic time in 1997 by including the first curvature correction [gasperini1997towards]. Their expanding solutions approach this phase from the vacuum, with a dilaton that continues to grow through the phase of constant curvature [gasperini1997towards]. Brustein and Richard Madden constructed an exit in 1998 with curvature corrections and quantum corrections whose signs they chose to violate the null energy condition [brustein1998model]. The Einstein frame geometry then bounces from contraction to expansion; further terms or radiation are needed to halt the dilaton, and the required correction coefficients were not derived from string theory [brustein1998model].¶Valerio Bozza, Gasperini, Massimo Giovannini, and Veneziano used a massive Kalb-Ramond axion to generate adiabatic curvature perturbations in 2002 and 2003 [bozza2002axions, bozza2003cmb]. The axion begins displaced from the minimum of its potential, oscillates until it dominates the energy density, and decays before nucleosynthesis [bozza2002axions, bozza2003cmb]. Through this curvaton mechanism, its initial isocurvature perturbations become curvature perturbations with the same spectral slope [bozza2003cmb]. The axion spectrum can be nearly flat even when the directly amplified metric perturbations have a steep blue spectrum; the observed microwave anisotropy constrains the axion displacement, the transition scale, and the evolution of the internal dimensions [bozza2003cmb].¶Gasperini combined the axion and microwave constraints with the relic graviton spectrum in 2016, finding allowed parameters whose gravitational radiation could reach the design sensitivity of ground and space interferometers [gasperini2016observable]. Modes that reenter during axion domination acquire an additional decrease with frequency, so the observed graviton spectrum depends on the evolution after the bounce [gasperini2016observable]. Gasperini found in 2017 that a slightly red axion spectrum selects growing string coupling for a vacuum with three expanding and six internal dimensions [gasperini2017initial]. The energy density of its perturbations becomes less important toward the past, so their backreaction imposes no beginning on that low energy phase [gasperini2017initial].¶Jérôme Quintin, Robert Hans Brandenberger, Gasperini, and Veneziano described a gas of black holes of string size in 2018, with pressureless matter in the string frame [quintin2018stringholes]. Curvature corrections of first order support an expanding phase with constant expansion rate and a dilaton linear in time [quintin2018stringholes]. The stability of the gas depends on the choice of corrected action [quintin2018stringholes]. Olaf Hohm and Barton Zwiebach classified the homogeneous corrections compatible with duality to every order in $\alpha'$ in 2019, for the metric, the antisymmetric tensor, and the dilaton [hohm2019duality]. They used field redefinitions to write the action with first time derivatives alone, leaving coefficients whose values depend on the particular string theory [hohm2019duality].¶Peng Wang, Houwen Wu, Haitang Yang, and Shuxuan Ying constructed regular homogeneous backgrounds in 2019 by choosing a series of curvature corrections that matches the known bosonic coefficients [wang2019nonsingular]. They extended the construction in 2020 so that further perturbative coefficients could be accommodated when known [wang2020construct]. The dilaton in these solutions continues to grow after the curvature bounce [wang2019nonsingular, wang2020construct]. Pietro Conzinu, Gasperini, and Giovanni Marozzi found in 2020 that an assumed decrease of the axion sound speed during the string phase can amplify small scale perturbations enough to form primordial black holes [conzinu2020blackholes]. Their abundance depends on the assumed sound speed and on the duration of the string phase [conzinu2020blackholes].¶Gasperini returned to quantum transitions between the vacuum branches in 2021, treating the cosmological wave function with the Wheeler-DeWitt equation [gasperini2021quantum]. An effective dilaton potential can scatter this wave function from a branch of growing curvature to one of decreasing curvature, with a nonzero transition probability even when the classical geometries stay disconnected [gasperini2021quantum]. The transition probability depends on the dilaton potential and on the incoming vacuum state [gasperini2021quantum].¶Gasperini and Veneziano characterized a class of regular bounces in 2023 through the Hamiltonian form of the duality invariant equations [gasperini2023nonsingular]. The expanding geometry contracts briefly in the string frame near the bounce, then approaches decelerated expansion in both conformal frames [gasperini2023nonsingular]. Gasperini and Veneziano chose the form of the curvature corrections, and their regular trajectories require a multivalued Lagrangian [gasperini2023nonsingular]. Li Song and Deyou Chen constructed further regular backgrounds that year, assuming convergence of a series with free parameters available to match later curvature coefficients [song2023solutions]. Tomas Codina, Hohm, and Zwiebach also showed that year that perturbative field redefinitions can remove every curvature correction from the isotropic homogeneous action [codina2023bianchi]. They emphasized that such perturbative field redefinitions need not preserve solutions that depend on the full series [codina2023bianchi].¶Conzinu, Giuseppe Fanizza, Gasperini, Eliseo Pavone, Luigi Tedesco, and Veneziano added a nonperturbative dilaton potential to the regular backgrounds in 2023 [conzinu2023vacuum]. For suitable potentials and initial conditions the dilaton settles at a finite value, and the geometry approaches an isotropic expansion even from anisotropic initial data [conzinu2023vacuum]. A zero potential minimum gives the late expansion of a universe filled with pressureless matter; a positive minimum can give de Sitter expansion [conzinu2023vacuum].¶Yang Jiang, Xi-Long Fan, and Qing-Guo Huang obtained upper limits on the pre big bang graviton spectrum from the first three observing runs of Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo in 2023 [jiang2023ligo]. Conzinu and Marozzi also followed primordial black hole formation through the axion dominated era that year, including the time required for collapse and the angular momentum of the collapsing regions [conzinu2023matter]. They found only a restricted region compatible with black hole dark matter and warned that the same models can overproduce lighter evaporating holes [conzinu2023matter]. Denis Bitnaya, Conzinu, and Marozzi found in 2024 that bulk viscosity can turn a gas of black holes of string size into an attractor for selected first order actions and equations of state [bitnaya2024stability]. Homogeneous perturbations oscillate around an allowed fixed point when the corrections are kept to all orders, under conditions on the effective coefficients [bitnaya2024stability].¶Ido Ben-Dayan, Gianluca Calcagni, Gasperini, Anupam Mazumdar, Pavone, Udaykrishna Thattarampilly, and Amresh Verma derived the minimal graviton spectrum with four independent parameters in 2024 [bendayan2024bouncing]. The parameters describe the string phase and the axion era, with the microwave amplitude fixing the curvature scale at the bounce [bendayan2024bouncing]. Some allowed spectra reach the projected sensitivities of LISA and the Einstein Telescope, but their nanohertz amplitude falls below the pulsar timing signal [bendayan2024bouncing]. Qin Tan, You Wu, and Lang Liu fitted a simpler spectrum to the NANOGrav 15-year data in 2024 and found weak evidence over a power law, without including the axion era or its microwave constraint [tan2025string]. The axion era and the microwave amplitude impose additional constraints on the minimal spectrum [tan2025string, conzinu2025nanograv].¶Stephen Angus and Shinji Mukohyama derived linear perturbation equations for the metric, dilaton, antisymmetric tensor, and matter in double field theory in 2025 [angus2025perturbations]. They solved the scalar perturbations outside the Hubble radius for several backgrounds, including the dilaton vacuum, at the lowest derivative order [angus2025perturbations]. Tan, Wu, and Liu found that the minimal graviton spectrum with four parameters could not fit the NANOGrav signal in their 2025 Bayesian analysis [tan2025nanograv]. Conzinu and coauthors matched the amplitude and frequency of the earlier fit that year by allowing the tensor and axion amplification to vary independently during the string phase, with the microwave and interferometer constraints imposed [conzinu2025nanograv].¶Conzinu, Gasperini, and Pavone supplied examples of this more general string phase in 2025 with radiation, unstable strings, or a gas of black holes of string size [conzinu2025nonminimal]. The sources alter the background and the amplification of its perturbations, allowing spectra compatible with the pulsar timing amplitude [conzinu2025nonminimal]. Shear viscosity changes the tensor perturbations without changing the axion perturbations, and can break the S-duality relation between their amplification [conzinu2025nonminimal].¶Tan, Zu-Cheng Chen, Wu, and Liu found no stochastic signal from this cosmology in the first three observing runs of Advanced LIGO and Advanced Virgo in an analysis published in 2026, and constrained the axion based spectrum [tan2026ligo]. Xoán Vilas Currás and Calcagni forecast the recovery of the cosmological parameters with LISA in 2026, including Galactic and extragalactic foregrounds [vilascurras2026lisa]. The simulated signals constrain different parameters according to which bends of the spectrum fall within the detector band [vilascurras2026lisa]. Gasperini examined the global horizons of regular bouncing geometries that year and found examples of the string bounce with neither particle nor event horizons [gasperini2026horizons]. The existence of either horizon depends on the full past and future evolution, including the bounce and both asymptotic branches [gasperini2026horizons].

coordinates.name: Synchronous

parameters.description: Exponent along $y$; with $\beta_1 + \beta_2 + \beta_3 = 1$ the dilaton is constant and the metric is Kasner's
Exponent along $z$; the condition leaves two of the three exponents free, and with all three negative space expands along every axis

coordinates.convention: We use coordinates $(t, x, y, z)$, with $t$ the proper time of the comoving observers, and evaluate the powers $(-t)^{2\beta_i}$ with $t$ in a fixed unit, so they are dimensionless and the lengths sit in $x$, $y$, and $z$. The dilaton is $\phi = (\beta_1 + \beta_2 + \beta_3 - 1)\ln(-t)$, and every component assumes $\beta_1^2 + \beta_2^2 + \beta_3^2 = 1$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

coordinates.name: Conformal Time

parameters.description: Exponent of the scale factor in conformal time, $k = \beta/(1 - \beta)$: $k = -1/(1 + \sqrt3)$ for the expanding member, $\beta = -1/\sqrt3$, and $k = 1/(\sqrt3 - 1)$ for the contracting one, $\beta = 1/\sqrt3$
Scale factor $(-t)^\beta$ in conformal time, a pure number that is one at $t = -1$, where $\eta = -(1 + k)$

coordinates.convention: We use the conformal time $\eta$ of the two members with $\beta_1 = \beta_2 = \beta_3 = \beta$, defined by $d\eta = dt/a$ and fixed by $-t = (-\eta/(1 + k))^{1 + k}$, and the same $x$, $y$, and $z$. The dilaton is $\phi = (2k - 1)\ln(-\eta/(1 + k))$, and the powers are read with $\eta$ in the unit of $t$. A dot in the geodesic equations is a derivative with respect to an affine parameter.

related.text: Kasner's vacuum is the member whose exponents also sum to one, where the dilaton is constant. Its time runs the other way, on $t > 0$ [lidsey2000superstring].

Rescaled by $e^{-\phi}$ to the Einstein frame, where the dilaton is a massless scalar field, each of these universes is Kasner's universe with a scalar field run backward in time [gasperini2003prebigbang]. The accelerating isotropic expansion becomes an accelerating contraction there.

Another vacuum of the metric and dilaton of string theory, flat in its string frame with the dilaton linear in time. Gabriele Veneziano noted that with a cosmological term in the string action the general solution tends to it in the far past [veneziano1991duality]. Its scale factors are all one, so the inversion of scale factors leaves it unchanged.

The static, charged black hole of the same low energy string theory, with a Maxwell field beside the dilaton, whose dilaton changes with distance from the hole. Here the dilaton changes with time alone, and with every exponent negative space expands faster and faster toward a singularity.
Bianchi type I, flat space with a scale factor of its own along each axis. The dilaton of low energy string theory makes each scale factor a power of time [gasperini2003prebigbang].

A flat universe of a massless scalar field in which the big bang is replaced by a bounce of loop quantum cosmology. Long before the bounce it contracts as $(-t)^{1/3}$, the Einstein frame of the isotropic expansion here [gasperini2003prebigbang].
